collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two neighbors who have not spoken in a month both start humming the same old song: keep singing, or walk away.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) fell out over a fence a month ago, and have not said a word to each other since. This evening they are both down at the stream, filling water pots, carefully not looking at each other. Then (subject) starts humming an old song, and without thinking, (friend) hums the harmony. They both stop. What now?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) starts again, a little louder. (friend) joins in. They get through the whole song, standing in the stream with their pots, and at the end neither of them says anything about the fence. They walk back to the village together. It is a start.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) picks up (friend.his/her) pot and leaves without a word. (subject) stands there a while, listening to the water. The fence is still between them. But the next evening, from across the village, (subject) hears someone humming the harmony, very quietly.
